holidays.name: National Compliment Day
holidays.description: A day for handing out kind words like confetti. Tell your barista their latte art is stunning, tell your coworker their spreadsheet is a masterpiece, and tell a stranger their jacket is fantastic. Bonus points for meaning it.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is widely listed on January 24 as a mid-winter nudge to spread cheer when the holiday glow has faded.
holidays.funFact: Research on compliments suggests that people consistently underestimate how good a compliment makes the receiver feel, so the person giving it often gets the smaller thrill.

holidays.name: National Beer Can Appreciation Day
holidays.description: A salute to the humble aluminum-and-steel vessel that keeps your brew crisp, portable, and picnic-ready. Today you're encouraged to pause before the pop-top and admire the engineering in your hand.
holidays.origin: It marks January 24, 1935, when canned beer first went on sale to the public in Richmond, Virginia. The Gottfried Krueger Brewing Company sold it as a test run.
holidays.funFact: Those first cans were made of steel and needed a church-key opener, because the pull tab wasn't invented until decades later.

holidays.name: Macintosh Computer Day
holidays.description: A nod to the beige, boxy computer with a smiling face that put a friendly mouse and icons on desks around the world. Tech fans mark the day by remembering the startup chime and the first friendly 'hello' on screen.
holidays.origin: Steve Jobs unveiled the original Apple Macintosh on January 24, 1984. Apple had teased it days earlier with a famous Super Bowl commercial.
holidays.funFact: The original Mac shipped with a built-in 9-inch black-and-white screen and just 128 KB of memory, which is far less than a single modern emoji image needs.
